subject: Insurance
title: Piracy and Insurance Premiums
description: A short lesson to help you apply Piracy and Insurance Premiums.

hook.text: Pirates didn't just steal cargo—they drove up insurance costs.

buildup.text: The Barbary pirates of North Africa terrorized Mediterranean shipping for centuries. Insurers priced the danger in.

discovery.text: Navies were partly funded by insurers who lobbied governments to protect trade routes. Insurance shaped military policy.

twist.text: Modern Somali piracy raised insurance costs 300% for ships passing the Gulf of Aden. The pattern hasn't changed.

climax.text: Insurance premiums are a mirror of global danger. Where risk rises, premiums follow—and they never lie.

punchline.text: Pirates raise premiums. Insurance prices the world's dangers.

quiz.question: How did piracy affect insurance?
options: Premiums rose significantly on dangerous routes
